newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with no reported sales of slaughter steers or heifers, feedlot sources said.
There were a few packer bids at $66.00, but they were passed by owners pricing cattle at $67.00, they said.

Most of this week's cattle were sold on Wednesday at $67.00, unchanged from last week. A few cattle sold Thursday at $66.00, but several feedlot sources said the sales were not indicative of the market.
Sales this week also not large enough to deplete showlists at Panhandle and Kansas feedlots, they said.
Week to date sales early Friday were at 70,400 head in the Panhandle and 69,300 in Kansas, USDA reported.
Showlists early in the week were estimated near 90,000 head in the Panhandle and 81,000 in Kansas, according to market sources.
Fed cattle next week were seen priced $68.00 to $69.00 amid ideas that beef prices had bottomed following declines since March 25, the market sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.09 to $0.30 per cwt, with heavyweight choice down $0.28 at $100.16, a decline of $4.05 since prices started falling.
